records.name: Women in GIS, Delaware Valley chapter
records.summary: The Delaware Valley chapter of Women in GIS, an international network for women who work with maps and location data. The chapter covers Philadelphia, southeastern Pennsylvania, southern New Jersey and northern Delaware, and offers networking for its members and other women in the field.
records.what_you_do: Meet other women who work with maps and location data through the chapter's networking. Some network events are for members only, and the wider network also runs mentoring programs.

schedule.text: The international network runs online sessions most months, including a monthly lightning talk series and topic groups. The Delaware Valley chapter lists no meeting dates.

cost.text: Yearly dues: $20 for students and early career members, $40 for professionals. A sustaining membership is $5 a month. Dues grants are available for those who need help.

first_step.how: Join through the Join Now button on the membership page, or send a message through the chapter contact link to ask about the next networking event.
first_step.basis: Member only events need a membership login, and dues come before you can see them. The chapter lists no meeting dates, and the site does not say whether non-members can attend chapter events.
first_step.what_to_expect: The chapter does not post its meetings on its page, so the first step is to ask. Most network events are one hour online sessions on Zoom, often at lunchtime, and the events page does not list a price for any of them.
first_visit_tips: Email the chapter first, since no chapter meeting is posted.
Students and early career members pay the lowest dues, $20 a year.
Ask about a dues grant if cost is a barrier; the site says grants are available.

records.notes: The Events page lists 16 dated events from 30 Sep to 6 Nov 2026, but none is a Delaware Valley chapter event (they are network wide or belong to the Georgia and Tampa Bay chapters). Status stays probably_active for that reason, and last_sign_of_life reflects the network events page. Dues come from the Join Us page. The About page says the network serves women in geospatial fields and their allies, so the community tag is kept as women for the membership. No page shows a physical meeting place, so no location is recorded.

records.name: Writers Room
records.summary: Drexel University's literary arts program for students, alumni and neighbors. It runs a monthly writing workshop, free readings, a writing course and community storytelling projects, and everything it does is free and open to all.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly Second Tuesday workshop, where Drexel students and neighbors share stories and build community together. You can also attend free events, join the mailing list, or take the WRIT290 writing course. Community projects such as Crossing Streets link West Philadelphia and Chinatown.

schedule.text: Second Tuesday is a monthly workshop on the second Tuesday of each month at the Dornsife Center for Neighborhood Partnerships. The site does not give a start time. The WRIT290 writing course meets on Wednesdays from 5 to 7:50 pm in fall and spring.

cost.text: Free. The site says everything it does is free and open to all, and donations help keep programs free.

first_step.how: Email writersroom@drexel.edu or call 215.571.3671 to ask for the start time and sign-up steps for the next Second Tuesday workshop.
first_step.basis: The site says everything is free and open to all, and it gives an email and phone number for questions. It does not say how to sign up for Second Tuesday or whether you must register in advance.
first_step.what_to_expect: Second Tuesday is a monthly workshop at the Dornsife Center for Neighborhood Partnerships, where Drexel students and neighbors take part together. The site does not say how long a session lasts, what time it starts, or whether you need to sign up in advance, so ask the team these questions before you go.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the start time and the room before you go, since the site does not list them.
The homepage newsletter form shows a notice that it may not be working yet, so email is the more reliable way to get updates.

records.notes: No page read gives the Second Tuesday start time, the sign-up rule, or whether neighbors may attend. One search found only 2016 and 2018 Drexel news items and an unrelated Boston group, so none of it was used. The Second Tuesday page says the workshop has run for 11 years, with no year given. The 2025 year appears only in the site copyright line and is not used as evidence. WRIT290 is offered with Drexel's English and Philosophy department; the page does not say whether community members can enroll or what it costs. Its enrollment form was not submitted.

records.name: Wyck Historic House and Garden
records.summary: Wyck is a National Historic Landmark house, garden and farm in Germantown, run by the Wyck Association. Visitors can walk the grounds for free during posted hours, take a house tour, or join the Home Farm Club to help grow food.
records.what_you_do: Walk the grounds and gardens during open hours and take a house tour. Join the Home Farm Club, a kitchen garden where you learn skills and help grow food, or come to a monthly Second Saturday workshop on gardening, cooking or history. Volunteers can sign up for the garden newsletter for tasks, train as house docents, or help with a committee, and you can become a member.

schedule.text: Grounds are free to walk Tuesday to Friday, 10 am to 4 pm, and Saturday, noon to 4 pm. House tours run Thursday to Saturday, noon to 4 pm (fall hours). The Home Farm Club meets on Tuesdays and Fridays in season, and Second Saturday workshops run monthly, mostly 11 am to 12:30 pm.

cost.text: Grounds and the Home Farm Club are free. Individual membership is $50 to $99 a year, or from $35 for the 19144 neighbor rate, and includes free unlimited regular tours. Some Second Saturday workshops charge a fee.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: take the Chestnut Hill West Regional Rail line to Tulpehocken station, then walk 10 to 15 minutes. The site also lists SEPTA buses 23, 65 and XH/81.

first_step.how: Walk onto the grounds during posted hours, or come to a Home Farm Club session on the Tuesday or Friday time posted for the season, entering through the Walnut Lane entrance. No registration is needed for the Home Farm Club.
first_step.basis: The Home Farm Club says no prior experience is needed and no registration is required, children can come with a parent, and each visit starts with short lessons. The site does not name a separate newcomer program, so this is a 4 rather than a 5.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Home Farm Club visit starts with a short lesson, then hands-on work in the kitchen garden, such as weeding, pruning and harvesting. There is no time commitment, and volunteers take home a share of the fresh produce. Most Second Saturday workshops run from 11 am to 12:30 pm and need an online sign up.
first_visit_tips: Enter the farm at the Walnut Lane entrance, as the site directs.
Free parking is on W. Walnut Lane, E. High Street and nearby side streets; metered spots are on Germantown Avenue.
For a Second Saturday workshop, sign up online early, since seats are limited and registration opens up to two weeks before.

records.notes: Visit hours are the fall hours the site posts, so check before a first visit. The getting-to-wyck page and the homepage say nothing about wheelchair access, elevators or accessible tours, so access.wheelchair is left out. The become a member button leads to a PayPal donation page; nothing was submitted. The Second Saturday series page uses the older name Home Farm Foodways Series in its web address. The Home Farm Club 2026 schedule starts April 7, 2026 and lists September and October sessions. Volunteer pages give no minimum age or time commitment. The site lists no paid jobs at this time.

records.name: Yes! And... Collaborative Arts
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that uses performing arts to build confidence, voice and community in children and teens from kindergarten through 12th grade. It runs fall to spring classes, summer camps, and Shadow Company, a year-round youth theater group for high schoolers.
records.what_you_do: Enroll a child in a fall to spring class or a summer camp, or have a high school student join Shadow Company at any time. Families can come to youth shows, and supporters can volunteer, sponsor or donate.

schedule.text: Classes run fall to spring. Silhouettes, a theater class for grades 5 to 8, meets monthly on Saturdays from 10 am to noon. Summer camps run each summer for grades K to 12. Shadow Company runs on a season from October through September, with monthly meetings for grades 9 to 12.

cost.text: Classes use a sliding scale, with listed direct costs of $160 to $365 per session, and lower tiers and full scholarships are available. One Silhouettes day can be bought alone for $31.25. Shadow Company has no fee. Camp prices are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Register a child for a class or camp through the online form linked on the program pages, or buy one Silhouettes drop-in day for $31.25. High school students can register for Shadow Company at any time through its year-round form.
first_step.basis: Anyone can register online for a class, camp, or Shadow Company. The site does not offer a free trial class and does not say beginners are welcome, but a single Silhouettes day can be bought for $31.25.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes meet at the main building at 21 W Washington Lane, and sessions run from one to three hours. Kids work with professional artists on singing, dancing, improv and sketches, and the classes we read about end with a showing or showcase for family and friends. Shadow Company meets monthly, and the site does not mention an audition for members.
first_visit_tips: Ask about scholarships before you pay: lower tiers and full scholarships exist, but the scholarship page gives no application steps, so call or email the group.
Plan to pay a deposit or the full fee when you register, since a spot is not held until you pay.
Check the refund rule first: no refunds within 5 days of the first session, or for missed sessions.

records.notes: The tier 1 summary said classes were year-round. The classes page lists fall to spring sessions, so the summary, schedule and what_you_do are corrected. Dated Variety Show, Stage Combat and Silhouettes dates are written without a year, so none is used. The 2026 auction fundraiser is written with its year but no month, so last_sign_of_life is left empty. Camp hours, camp prices and camp registration steps are not on the site. Shadow Company questions go to shadow@yesandcamp.org, as published on that page. No accessibility details appear on any page read. The one time Fringe show is not in the schedule because it has no date.

notes: Four records written, one per batch group. 20 WebFetch calls in total (cap 6 per group) and 1 WebSearch of the 1 allowed. No page was blocked and no rate limiting was seen. Writers Room Second Tuesday start time and sign-up rule were not found on any page or in the one search, so they are left out. Women in GIS is probably_active because its dated 2026 events are network wide and online, not Delaware Valley chapter events. No leads_only added: the groups named only unlinked or non-community items (Second Story Collective, Friends events at Wyck, the FringeArts Festival), none with its own community-group website in the batch pages read.
